title: Oxygen Sensor Signals Swapped (Bank 1 Sensor 1 / Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: On a V-type engine there is an upstream oxygen sensor for each side. The computer has noticed that the bank 1 and bank 2 upstream sensor signals appear to be swapped.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Possible rough running or poor fuel economy
May fail an emissions test

causes.name: Sensor connectors plugged into the wrong side after a repair
Sensor harnesses routed or wired incorrectly
Wrong sensors installed on each bank

checks: Check if oxygen sensors or exhaust parts were recently replaced
Trace each sensor wire to make sure it plugs into the correct connector
Watch both sensor readings while making one bank richer with a scan tool
fix: Usually correcting the connections or wiring so each sensor plugs into its own side.

title: Oxygen Sensor Signals Swapped (Bank 1 Sensor 2 / Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: On engines with two exhaust sides, the computer has noticed that the downstream (after the catalytic converter) oxygen sensor signals for bank 1 and bank 2 appear to be swapped.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
May fail an emissions test

causes.name: Downstream sensor connectors swapped after a repair
Sensor harnesses routed or wired incorrectly
Wrong sensors installed on each side

checks: Check if oxygen sensors or converters were recently replaced
Trace each downstream sensor wire to its correct connector
fix: Usually correcting the sensor connections so each one plugs into its own side.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
plain: Oxygen sensors have a built-in heater so they start working soon after a cold start. The computer found a fault, such as an open circuit, in the heater circuit of the third, furthest-downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Failed heater inside the oxygen sensor
Blown fuse for the oxygen sensor heaters
Damaged or melted wiring near the exhaust
Corroded or loose sensor connector
Engine computer heater driver fault

checks: Check the oxygen sensor heater fuse
Inspect the sensor wiring for melted or rubbed-through spots near the exhaust
Measure the heater resistance at the sensor and compare to spec
fix: Most often a new oxygen sensor. If the fuse is blown, find the short that blew it before replacing the sensor.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control "A" Circuit/Open
plain: The boost control system (usually a wastegate or variable vane actuator) sets how much pressure the turbo or supercharger makes. The computer found an open or broken connection in the "A" boost control circuit.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Loss of power or slow acceleration
Engine may go into limp mode

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector to the boost control solenoid or actuator
Failed boost control solenoid or electronic actuator
Blown fuse or poor power feed
Engine computer driver fault

checks: Inspect the boost control solenoid or actuator connector and wiring
Measure the solenoid resistance and compare to spec
Command the actuator with a scan tool and watch it move
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new boost control solenoid or actuator.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control "A" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The boost control system (usually a wastegate or variable vane actuator) sets how much pressure the turbo or supercharger makes. The computer found a response that does not match what it commanded in the "A" boost control circuit.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Loss of power or slow acceleration
Engine may go into limp mode

causes.name: Sticking wastegate or variable vane mechanism
Faulty boost control solenoid or actuator
Cracked or leaking vacuum or boost hose
Wiring or connector problem

checks: Inspect vacuum and boost hoses for cracks or loose clamps
Check the wastegate or vane linkage for binding
Compare commanded and actual boost with a scan tool
fix: Often a sticking wastegate or vane linkage, a leaking hose, or a failed boost control solenoid.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Turbine Overspeed
plain: The computer has calculated or measured that the turbocharger is spinning faster than its safe limit. This can quickly wear out or damage the turbo.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may go into limp mode
Whistling or unusual turbo noise
Possible black smoke

causes.name: Wastegate or variable vanes stuck in the high-boost position
Boost leak making the turbo work harder
Faulty boost pressure or turbo speed sensor
Restricted air filter or intake

checks: Check for boost leaks at hoses and the intercooler
Check the wastegate or vane actuator for sticking
Compare boost pressure readings with a scan tool
fix: Fix whatever is making the turbo overspin, often a stuck wastegate or vane actuator or a boost leak. Avoid hard driving until repaired.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
plain: Oxygen sensors have a built-in heater so they start working soon after a cold start. The computer found a fault, such as an open circuit, in the heater circuit of the upstream (before the catalytic converter) oxygen sensor on bank 2.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
Fuel economy may drop slightly, mostly after cold starts

causes.name: Failed heater inside the oxygen sensor
Blown fuse for the oxygen sensor heaters
Damaged or melted wiring near the exhaust
Corroded or loose sensor connector
Engine computer heater driver fault

checks: Check the oxygen sensor heater fuse
Inspect the sensor wiring for melted or rubbed-through spots near the exhaust
Measure the heater resistance at the sensor and compare to spec
fix: Most often a new oxygen sensor. If the fuse is blown, find the short that blew it before replacing the sensor.
drive: Usually you can keep driving normally and schedule a repair; the heater only helps the oxygen sensor warm up quickly. Get it checked sooner if the engine starts running rough, other codes appear, or you smell fuel. The car may not pass an emissions or inspection test until it's fixed.
test_first: Check the O2 heater fuse first, then measure heater resistance and check power and ground at the connector. Inspect the wiring near the exhaust for melting before replacing the sensor.

title: HO2S Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
plain: The computer checks the resistance of the heater inside each oxygen sensor. The heater in the upstream (before the catalytic converter) sensor on bank 1 measured outside its normal range.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
May fail an emissions or readiness test

causes.name: Worn or failed heater inside the oxygen sensor
Wrong or aftermarket sensor with a different heater rating
High resistance from a corroded connector or damaged wiring

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Measure the heater resistance and compare to spec
Make sure any replacement sensor is the correct part for the vehicle
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor of the correct type.

title: "B" Camshaft Profile Control Performance/Stuck Off (Bank 1)
plain: Some engines can switch between two camshaft lobe shapes. On bank 1, the computer found the "B" cam switching system not switching properly or stuck in its off position.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Less power at higher engine speeds
Possible lower fuel economy

causes.name: Low, dirty or wrong-grade engine oil
Sticking cam profile switching solenoid
Low oil pressure to the switching mechanism
Worn or sticking cam follower or locking pin

checks: Check the oil level and condition
Check oil pressure
Inspect the switching solenoid and its screen for sludge
fix: Often an oil change and a new switching solenoid. Mechanical wear inside the valvetrain is less common.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control "B" Supply Voltage Circuit Low
plain: The "B" boost control actuator needs a steady power supply to work. The computer found that the supply voltage to it is too low.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Loss of power or limp mode

causes.name: Blown fuse or failed relay for the actuator
Damaged power or ground wiring
Corroded connector
Weak battery or charging problem

checks: Check the fuse and relay feeding the actuator
Measure supply voltage at the actuator connector
Inspect the wiring harness for damage
fix: Usually a fuse, relay or wiring repair; sometimes a new boost actuator.
